newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian bond yields off as U.S. gets PPI boost.
newsitem.headline: Australian bond yields off as U.S. gets PPI boost.

text.p: Australian bond yields were lower in early trading, responding to the advance in U.S. Treasuries following a 0.6 percent drop in the April U.S. PPI, its largest fall in 3-1/2 years.

However, the U.S. rally was restrained somewhat with the market still concerned over the outcome of next Tuesday's Federal Open Market Committee meeting and on continued weakness in the U.S. dollar against the yen.
The dollar fell further in early Sydney trading to 116.55 yen, its lowest level since January.
The April U.S. CPI is due later on Thursday.
The firmer tone in the U.S. helped domestic bonds shake off some of its post-budget gloom, although the June 10-year bond futures contract is finding stiff resistance at 92.280.

The contract had dropped to 92.180 amid disappointment over Tuesday's 1997/98 budget, retreating from a 11-week high of 92.370 just prior to the statement, with market having anticipated a much tighter outcome.

The market will be keen to hear any comment from Reserve Bank governor Ian Macfarlane when he addresses a conference in Melbourne at 12.00 p.m. (0200 GMT) in response to the budget, but he not expected to retreat from his on-hold policy stance.

Yields spreads to the dollar bloc were little changed in early trading, remaining at Wednesday's slightly wider levels against the U.S. New Zealand bonds slightly outperformed, taking confirmation from the RBNZ that its policy stance had been unchanged since December in its stride.
